newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to press Chechen leader over hostages.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to press Chechen leader over hostages.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin plans to press the leader of Chechnya over the fate of Russian journalists and other hostages held in the breakaway region, the Kremlin said on Friday.

Presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Russian and Chechen officials would meet on Saturday to arrange talks between Yeltsin and Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov in Moscow. He did not say when the talks were likely to take place.

Yeltsin, who discussed preparations for the meeting with Kremlin security official Ivan Rybkin on Friday, says he wants to meet Maskhadov in the "near future" and the meeting is widely expected in the next few days.
"The (questions) will surely include the revival of the Chechen economy, federal financial support for the republic, the seizure of people in Chechnya," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.
"The president will naturally inquire about what Chechen law enforcement agencies are doing to free the journalists."

Yeltsin has sought to tackle Russia's most pressing problems since returning on August 5 from a month-long vacation. Chechnya, which dogged his first presidential term which ended last year, is high on his list.

Talks on normalising relations are stalled over Chechnya's status, an issue left unresolved when Russia withdrew its troops a year ago after nearly 21 months of fighting over the North Caucasus region's independence drive.

Maskhadov, who commanded the guerrilla forces which humiliated Russia's troops, says Chechnya is already independent. The Kremlin has ruled out full independence but promised the region wide autonomy.
Yastrzhembsky said last week Russia was also concerned that documents signed under a peace deal with Chechnya were not being put into effect.
Relations have been further complicated by dozens of kidnaps in the last few months in Chechnya and nearby areas which highlighted the lawlessness in the region.
Several Russian and foreign journalists have been abducted and two Britons, five French people, one Slovak, a Yugoslav and a German are among those still held in the North Caucasus.
The Chechen authorities have proved unable to halt the kidnaps, but one official said they had found the whereabouts of a group which kidnapped several Russian journalists.

Magomed Magomadov, head of a special team investigating the abductions, told RIA news agency the kidnappers had told they would be stormed by an assault squad unless they released the journalists in the next two days.
